Use case: style-transfer. Input image 1 is our own distant grove painting, the EXACT composition and geometry reference. Paint the same view as a low-polygon game renders it, with ZERO textures.
Keep the camera, horizon, coastline outline, water occupying the lower third, hill silhouette, curved boulevard, all ruined building landmarks, the broken seawall at middle right, and the positions, sizes, types and lean directions of the palm groves recognizably matched to image 1. This must be a directly comparable simplified version of that same place, not a new scene. No foreground tree or new near bank.
Simplify EVERY palm into a narrow polygonal trunk of only 3–5 visible faces and a radial star crown of just 6–9 solid flat green pointed bent blades. Angular feather-like blade silhouettes with broad bases tapering to long points, 2–3 segments for the arch and droop, no tiny leaflet texture, no noise. Royals use slender pale-grey straight posts, a short green crownshaft block and compact elevated crown stars. Coconuts have 3–4-segment thin grey-brown curved posts with broad loose hanging star crowns. Retain height variation, missing crown sectors, irregular spacing and sunny vs shaded crown colors. At this native image size most palms just 20–50 pixels tall; still unmistakable as palms.
Each polygon is a SINGLE UNIFORM SOLID COLOR. No photographic detail, no bark rings, no stipple, no brush grain, no grass texture, no sand texture, no cracks or rock texture, no ocean ripples, no gradients on objects, no smooth specular highlights. Terrain consists of broad flat ochre/sage planar facets; ruins a few pale warm grey blocks with deep flat blue-grey openings; sea broad clean flat turquoise/teal polygons; clouds a few broad flat warm cream and cool lavender polygon shapes; distant hills flat muted blue layers. Crisp edges and controlled believable flat-shaded lighting, long clean polygon cast shadows, handsome restrained palette. It should expose how few shapes are necessary for a distant palm silhouette to work, not merely put a polygon filter over the textured image. No text, labels or watermark. Largest available native landscape PNG.
